sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a house in Centerville, Ohio?
sections.html:
A cash purchase closes fastest, and a listing usually earns the stronger price. Centerville is a core suburb of the Dayton area, so a house in good order can draw buyers on the open market.

  • Agent listing: suited to a maintained house in a sought-after school zone. Plan on staging, showings, and a buyer's inspection.
  • As-is cash sale: sensible when the roof, the mechanicals, or the finishes need money you would rather not spend before selling.
  • Private sale: possible if you already have a buyer lined up. A written contract and a title company still protect both sides.

Eighty-five percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, per the Census Bureau, so most sellers here know their houses well and can answer a buyer's questions about them.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Centerville homes?
sections.html:
Centerville skews older and owner-occupied. The 2020 census put the median age at 48.8, with 29.5% of residents 65 or older and 70.4% of occupied homes lived in by owners. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 25,194 residents is 4.2% above its 2020 base.

sections.h2: How old is Centerville, and what does that mean for a house here?
sections.html:
Aaron Nutt, Benjamin Archer, and Benjamin Robbins surveyed the area in February 1796. The state recognized Centerville in 1803, it was platted in 1805, and it incorporated as a town in 1830. It became a city on December 2, 1968, and the post office changed the spelling from Centreville to Centerville in 1900.

Early settlers built log houses and then limestone ones. Wikipedia says nearly 100 stone buildings stood along local streets in the nineteenth century, many survive, and the city holds the largest collection of early stone houses in Ohio. If your house is in the historic core around the Heart of Centerville, ask the city whether review rules cover exterior changes before you promise a buyer a renovation.

Away from the old center, suburban growth filled in the map. School enrollment passed 6,800 in 1969, and Centerville High School moved to its present campus in 1973, which hints at when much of the city was built.

sections.h2: How does a Centerville deed reach the Montgomery County record?
sections.html:
A small piece of the city lies in Greene County, so confirm the county on your tax bill first. For most Centerville parcels the deed goes through Montgomery County's Auditor, whose Deed Transfer Department adds a transfer or no-transfer stamp, and then to the Recorder.

The Recorder's FAQ says a deed needs the names of buyer and seller, the legal description, the seller's signature, and a notary block. It says documents are recorded the same business day they arrive, once the Auditor has stamped them. Items that need a No Transfer stamp, such as transfer on death designations and easements, are mailed or walked through the Auditor's department. Ask the Recorder for the current fee schedule before you file.

  • Revised Code 319.202 makes the seller pay the transfer fee.
  • Paying off a mortgage creates no new deed. The lender records a release, viewable on the county's online records search.
  • The county holds roughly 230,000 parcels, so quote your parcel number on every form.

sections.h2: How do I contest my Centerville property value?
sections.html:
Montgomery County owners file with the Board of Revision from January 1 through March 31, stating the value they want and the reason. Under Revised Code 5715.19 the date can run later when first-half collection closes after March 31.

The complainant carries the burden of proof. The county lists acceptable evidence as a sale of the property within three years, a recent appraisal, sales of similar nearby homes, a realtor's market analysis, and itemized repair estimates. Lists of other properties' assessed values, comments on neighbors' upkeep, and tax rate complaints do not count.

Tax year 2025 hearings ran by video or phone and lasted 10 to 20 minutes per property. A decision arrives by mail within 90 days, and either side then has 30 days to appeal to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the county Court of Common Pleas. A changed value holds until the next countywide update, which comes every three years unless the property is rebuilt or damaged.

sections.h2: What does Ohio's condition disclosure form require of a Centerville seller?
sections.html:
Revised Code 5302.30 has sellers of one to four unit homes describe the water supply, sewage system, roof, foundation, walls, floors, and known hazards on a state form. A buyer who first receives it after signing the contract can back out within three business days.

Transfers by an estate fiduciary, between spouses, to a lineal relative, or by an heir who did not live in the home the previous year are exempt. Centerville is prone to tornadoes, floods, and severe storms according to Wikipedia, so tell a buyer about any storm or water damage you know of.

sections.h2: Which schools, hospitals, and amenities draw buyers to Centerville?
sections.html:
The Centerville City School District has two primary schools, six elementary schools, three middle schools, Centerville High School, and an alternative high school. The Washington-Centerville Public Library lists more than 380,000 items.

Miami Valley Hospital South opened in 2007 as an outpatient site with an emergency department and grew into a full hospital with 60 beds by 2013, on a campus beside Interstate 675. Wikipedia names it the largest employer in the city, with retail and health care as the biggest job categories. The council-manager government has a seven-member council elected at large, and the Town Hall Theatre downtown dates to 1908. The Census lists 2022 retail sales of $44,802 per resident.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Centerville sale?
faqs.a: Mostly Montgomery County, with a small portion of the city in Greene County. The county on your deed and tax bill has the auditor, treasurer, and recorder who process your paperwork.

faqs.q: Does a historic stone house in Centerville need a review before I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the city's planning and zoning office whether your address falls in a historic area with review rules. Settle that question before you promise a buyer exterior changes.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the transfer fee in Centerville?
faqs.a: The seller. Revised Code 319.202 places the fee on the grantor, and your closing statement will show the figure.

faqs.q: When can Montgomery County owners file a value complaint?
faqs.a: From January 1 to March 31 each year. Send evidence of market value to the county's evidence portal at least 10 days before the hearing.

faqs.q: Do I fill out the disclosure form for an inherited Centerville house?
faqs.a: Often not. Revised Code 5302.30 exempts estate fiduciaries and heirs who did not live in the home the previous year. If you lived there, complete it. A title company or attorney can confirm which case fits you.
